auditor_value: (a) t = 7/6 s ≈ 1.17 s; (b) 4 m/s to the left (−4 m/s); (c) 1 kg block: 77/6 m ≈ 12.83 m to the left; 2 kg block: displacement 7/12 m ≈ 0.58 m to the left (path length 25/12 m ≈ 2.08 m, since it reverses at t = 0.5 s)

findings.note: 14/6 s = 2.33 s, not 1.17 s. Step 4 correctly finds t = 21/18 = 7/6 s; the fraction in the final answer is doubled and contradicts its own decimal. A student copying 14/6 s loses the mark.
The line as printed is false: 3(14/6) − 3(7/6)² = 7 − 49/12 = 35/12, not −7/12. The time inside the first term is doubled; with t = 7/6 s the result −7/12 m is right.

findings.quote: the 2 kg block displaces 7/12 m ≈ 0.58 m
findings.note: The served question asks how far each block travels. The 2 kg block reverses direction at t = 0.5 s (v = 3 − 6t = 0), so its path length is 0.75 m + 4/3 m = 25/12 m ≈ 2.08 m, while its displacement is 7/12 m. The solution silently answers displacement without naming the difference; for the 1 kg block the two coincide (77/6 m) because it never reverses.
findings.fix: the 2 kg block's displacement is 7/12 m ≈ 0.58 m to the left; because it stops and reverses at t = 0.5 s, the distance it travels is 0.75 m + 4/3 m = 25/12 m ≈ 2.08 m

question_defect: Part (c) says 'how far ... each travel', which reads as distance; the 2 kg block reverses direction before sliding stops, so distance (25/12 m) and displacement (7/12 m) differ for it. The wording should say either 'displacement' or 'distance travelled'.
